name: Clutch-luck stock: break points and tiebreaks beyond the match's own point rates
definition: Per player, over completed matches with a box score in the 365 days before this one, sum with a 13-week half-life (no shrinkage) three residuals against that match's own serve-point rates p_s (player) and p_o (opponent) under iid points: BP saved - faced*p_s; BP converted - chances*(1-p_o); tiebreaks won - played*q with q = p_s(1-p_o)/[p_s(1-p_o)+(1-p_s)p_o]. Composite = mean of the three standardised stocks; A - B; expected sign negative.
mechanism: Break-point and tiebreak over-performance does not persist (luck), yet it moves W/L records, rankings, Elo and the 'clutch' narrative; the model's raw BP rates mix this luck with serving skill; the close over-rates men's BP saving in every era (edge_anatomy), consistent with luck read as skill.
coverage_note: Box scores: ATP tour and Challenger >=99% every season 2010-26; WTA tour 84-88% in 2013-15 then >=96%; WTA 125 >=99% from 2016; ITF none before 2025 (R1 coverage_box_end.json, outcome-free); tiebreak counts present ~99% where a box score exists (<=2024)
model_overlap: medium (form_bp_saved, form_bp_conv, iosO_bp_saved, form_first_won, form_second_won); the orthogonal-part step decides
pool_rows: U-207 (bp_over: men constant, shrinkage K infinite), U-278, U-094, U-253
prior_evidence: Sackmann 2012 'The Luck of the Tiebreak': year-to-year correlation 'almost exactly zero' (ATP 1991-2012, >=15 TBs; R1 checked); Sackmann 2015 BP non-persistence (WTA; repo note); Kovalchik & Ingram 2016 (ATP 2011-15: tiebreak effect on serve points -0.06 pp n.s.); Kovalchik & Reid 2018 (BP won 'negligible'); repo: pool's men's bp_over K infinite (no persistent variance; src/eda/feature_interactions/inventory/build_inventory.py); edge_anatomy 2013-24 men BP saved vs price z -1.6 (long memory), -2.3 (two-week)
exposed_2025_26: partly: motivated by edge_anatomy's 2025-26 ledger of the in-model BP-saved rates (men z -3.9, -2.8), read by the lead and R1; the residual itself never read
notes: Same family as B2's PS01/PS03 (S2b building). Kill: split-half persistence of the residual > 0.3 (skill, not luck), or the close's own loading on it with no residual beta; likely unresolved alone on Look A (MDE ~0.064 per RMS unit), so register inside a group.

name: Break-point luck piece
definition: RS01's first two residuals only (BP saved - faced*p_s; BP converted - chances*(1-p_o)), per 100 break-point opportunities, 13-week half-life, unshrunk; A - B.
mechanism: As RS01; the part most directly tied to the close's over-rating of men's BP saving.
coverage_note: Box scores: ATP tour and Challenger >=99% every season 2010-26; WTA tour 84-88% in 2013-15 then >=96%; WTA 125 >=99% from 2016; ITF none before 2025 (R1 coverage_box_end.json, outcome-free)
prior_evidence: As RS01 (Sackmann 2015; Kovalchik & Reid 2018; pool K infinite; edge_anatomy 2013-24)
notes: Member of RS01.

name: Tiebreak luck piece
definition: Tiebreaks won minus sum over tiebreaks played of q(p_s, p_o) from each match's own serve-point rates, last 52 weeks (13-week half-life), plus tiebreaks played per match as exposure; A - B.
mechanism: Tiebreak wins are near coin flips but count fully in records, rankings and Elo; the model has no tiebreak input.
coverage_note: tiebreak counts present ~99% where a box score exists (<=2024)
model_overlap: low (no tiebreak input in the model)
prior_evidence: Sackmann 2012 (r ~0, R1 checked) and 2019 (two extra tiebreak wins ~ one match win); Kovalchik & Ingram 2016
exposed_2025_26: partly: raw tiebreak rates (U-207) were scored on 2025-26 by the predictability diagnostic; this residual not
notes: Member of RS01; B2's PS01.

name: Deciding-set luck piece
definition: Deciding sets won minus sum of the iid probability of winning a set at that match's own serve-point rates, over deciding sets played in the last 52 weeks; A - B.
mechanism: Deciding-set records regress strongly toward 45% + 0.2 x straight-set record; bettors read them as nerve.
coverage_note: Box scores: ATP tour and Challenger >=99% every season 2010-26; WTA tour 84-88% in 2013-15 then >=96%; WTA 125 >=99% from 2016; ITF none before 2025 (R1 coverage_box_end.json, outcome-free)
prior_evidence: Sackmann 2014/2024 ('three-set win% = 45% + 20% x two-set win%'; 36% three-setters vs 44% predicted, ATP 2014)
exposed_2025_26: partly: U-207's deciding-set form was scored on 2025-26 by the predictability diagnostic (onM men -0.039, worse)
notes: Weakest member of the luck family.

name: Load spike against the player's own normal (acute:chronic ratio)
definition: log(G14 / max(Gch, floor)): G14 = games played (singles at every level, doubles where held) in the 14 days before this match's earliest start es; Gch = mean 14-day games over days 15-70 before; floor = tour median 14-day games of active players; plus a flag for ratio >= 1.5; A - B.
mechanism: The close and the model see absolute recent load (sets_14d), not load relative to the player's own normal; spikes cause injury and flat play before any news shows; the 12-day Masters (2023, 2025) raised spikes; record retirements in 2025.
coverage_note: Every level 2010-26 (lower-level dates are windows); minutes partial below tour level
pool_rows: U-161 (ACWR, never screened), U-139, U-141, U-156
prior_evidence: Kovalchik 2020 PLoS One: cumulative load raises competition time-loss, HR 1.05 [1.01, 1.10] per 1,000 games, magnified with age (389 ATP players, 55,773 weeks; R1 checked); Amor-Salamanca et al. 2025 review: acute:chronic ratio >= 1.3-1.5 strongest external injury predictor; repo: B9a odometer x age z2 +2.52 (2022-24)
exposed_2025_26: partly: the schedule-and-body family's 2025-26 strength (edge_anatomy) shaped the choice; the ratio never read
notes: Kill: orthogonal part near zero, or no within-player effect of spikes on next-match points won vs own norm (gate on <=2024).

name: Season load x age
definition: Games played in the last 52 weeks relative to the field's walk-forward norm (tour, week, ranking band), times max(0, age - 27), with an autumn (Sep-Nov) indicator; A - B.
mechanism: Older players recover more slowly from accumulated load; the close prices age uniformly.
coverage_note: Every level 2010-26
prior_evidence: Kovalchik 2020 (load effect magnified with age); Palau et al. 2024 (lower tiers: +31% retirement risk per 5 years of mean age); retirement rate doubles every 5 years after 27 (Baiget/Casals group, university news); repo B9a z1 +0.10, z2 +2.52
notes: Member of RS05's group (scout #6).

name: Turnaround in hours, late finish, doubles since the last singles match
definition: H = hours from the end of the player's previous match (singles or doubles) to this match's scheduled start (end = Flashscore end_utc where present, else start_utc + Stage 0 minutes; doubles have start times only, so start + a typical duration); features min(H, 48) A - B, flag H < 20, previous finish after 23:00 local time, doubles matches since the last singles match.
mechanism: Books and models count days and sets, not clock hours; late finishes and same-day doubles are invisible in day counts.
data_paths: data/studies/match_timing/links/*.parquet (start_utc); data/studies/match_timing/links/flashscore_records.parquet (end_utc); data/studies/predictability_diagnostic/stage0_matches.parquet (minutes); data/dump/points/tennislive/listed.parquet (doubles start_utc, discipline); venue time zones from the gazetteer (to build)
coverage_note: start_utc: ATP main draw >=98.6% every season 2010-26; WTA 65-72% 2010-17, >=93% 2018-26. Flashscore end: ATP 90-99% to 2024, 16% (2025), 11% (2026); WTA 65-86% to 2024, 99% (2025), 37% (2026). Stage 0 minutes: ATP ~99% (2015: 52%), WTA >=93% from 2016 (none before). TennisLive finished_at is a '0' placeholder on 99.98% of listings: not a source (R1 coverage_clock.json, coverage_box_end.json, coverage_finish_fields.json)
prior_evidence: Turner et al. 2022 (lab, 12 players: max serve 10.5 km/h lower at 20:00 than 14:00); Ashman et al. 2010 (NBA back-to-backs vs spreads); Smith et al. 2013 (NFL circadian vs Las Vegas spread); Goossens et al. 2015 (Slams: previous-match sets); ATP 2025 late-finish rules (post-midnight finishes 50 -> 39)
notes: Same as B1's RB03/RB04 (S2a building). Scheduled start is published the evening before (WTA order of play released ~19:00). Kill: no within-player effect of H < 20 h on next-match points won vs own norm (<=2024).

name: Doubles load at the same event
definition: Doubles matches and sets the player played at this event, and in the 3 days before this singles match's scheduled start; A - B.
mechanism: Singles histories, ratings and most bettors ignore doubles minutes.
data_paths: data/raw/public_dump/sackmann_archive/atp/atp_matches_doubles_2010-2020.csv (event-level dates); data/dump/points/tennislive/listed.parquet (2018-26, start times only; finish field empty)
coverage_note: Men 2010-26 (event-level only to 2017); women 2018-26; TennisLive doubles: tour ~1,600-1,950 a year, Slams 504, Challengers 2,150-3,200; no doubles finish times (use start + typical duration, or count only doubles started >= 3 h before the singles start)
prior_evidence: No published study found (lane L1); B1 measured one player with doubles in the prior 7 days in 30-38% of frame matches 2018-24
notes: Same as B1's RB01 (S2a building); name linking needed (TennisLive 'A / B' members).

name: Draw shadow: a dominant player still alive, and the next-round shadow
definition: Dominant = as-of overall Elo >= 100 points above the field's 3rd-best entrant at the event's start; S = 1[another dominant player is still alive at es] x 1[player in Elo top 20, not dominant]; N = 1[a dominant player is the projected next-round opponent]; reverse term for players outside the top 50; each A - B.
mechanism: Effort and psychology in elimination draws respond to the draw beyond the current match; prices are set match-up by match-up; dominance concentrated again in 2024-26 (men).
data_paths: data/studies/predictability_diagnostic/stage0_matches.parquet (round, match_num, draw_size, player ids); data/studies/match_timing/timing.parquet (es, lf); Elo history (the model's Elo builder)
coverage_note: Both tours 2013-26 (main tour)
prior_evidence: Creutzburg 2024 (HCED WP 79; journal 2026): top-20 non-superstar players -3.4 pp win probability while a superstar is in the draw, more if he is the likely next opponent; players outside the top 50 +4.1 pp (n.s. with more events); ATP 2004-19, 27,366 matches, rank-difference, round, tournament and player-season FEs, no odds (R1 checked); Deutscher, Neuberg & Thiem 2023 JEP (stronger with several superstars, vanishes once they are out); Babington et al. 2020 (no effect in golf, skiing)
notes: Papers name the superstars (Federer, Nadal, Djokovic, Murray); the Elo definition is R1's so women and 2020-26 can be tested. Brown & Minor 2014 (Mgmt Sci) cited by Creutzburg, not read. Kill: no effect in 2013-19 with Elo (not rankings) as the control.

name: Player's own translation ratio from lower levels to the tour
definition: Men: opponent-adjusted total points won at Challenger level / at tour level over the last 36 months, shrunk toward the walk-forward global factor (~1.095) by matches at the scarcer level; women: WTA 125 vs tour; feature (ratio - global) x U-330's lower-level share; A - B.
mechanism: Rankings, Elo and a global level translation discount every player alike; the close under-rates arrivals from lower levels (growing by era); players whose lower-level form translates unusually are misjudged.
coverage_note: Men's Challenger box scores >=99% 2010-26; WTA 125 >=99% from 2016; women's ITF box only 2025-26
model_overlap: medium (the men's level layer; IOS profiles)
prior_evidence: Sackmann 2018: Challenger-to-tour factor 1.086-1.103 by year (2012-17); player ratios 0.982 (Ebden) to 1.180 (F. Mayer); persistence not tested (R1 checked); Sackmann 2025: Elo-market gaps mostly from thin lower-level data; repo U-330 beta beside the average close +0.13 [+0.07, +0.19] 2013-24 (500s +0.41, 1000s -0.02); current best leaves +0.12 [+0.03, +0.21] 2020-24
notes: Published support is thin; the project's U-330 carries it. Kill: split-half persistence of the ratio < 0.2, or no gain beside U-330.

name: Ranking stakes: points to defend and distance to a threshold
definition: (a) Ranking points the player earned at this event last year (Stage 0 + the tours' points tables) / current points; (b) signed distance in places to the nearest live threshold at the match date (top 100/104 Slam entry, top 32 Slam seeding, Finals-race top 8 in Sep-Nov); (c) points for winning this round / points gap to that threshold; A - B.
mechanism: Tournament theory: effort follows each player's marginal stake; prices reflect level and round, not individual stakes; 2026 rules (18 counting results, fewer mandatory 500s) shift stakes.
data_paths: data/studies/predictability_diagnostic/stage0_match_players.parquet (rank, rank_points); data/studies/predictability_diagnostic/stage0_matches.parquet (round, level); Sackmann weekly rankings (to 8 Jun 2026); TML ATP rankings (31 Aug 2026); Wikipedia edition pages (seeds' points before/dropped/after)
coverage_note: Men's weekly rankings to Aug 2026; women's 2025-26 weekly rankings need the WTA API or Wikipedia
prior_evidence: Gilsdorf & Sukhatme 2008 (ATP 2001: larger prize gaps raise the stronger player's win probability); Lallemand, Plasman & Rycx 2008 (WTA); Sunde 2009 (ATP semis/finals); Sackmann 2013 (seeds 61% vs 70% at 250s the week before a Slam, raw); repo B-MOTIV z1 +2.39, z2 +0.49
notes: Overlaps B3's MP-07-09 (S2c building MP-08/09). Wikipedia probe: receipts/wikipedia/.

name: Heat stress: heat-weighted recent load, and heat x age
definition: Outdoor WBGT at the venue and scheduled hour from hourly temperature, humidity, wind and radiation (Liljegren; Open-Meteo); (i) sum of minutes x max(0, WBGT - 25 C) over the last 3 days, A - B; (ii) WBGT at this match x (age_A - age_B); (iii) a 2026+ ATP heat-rule indicator.
mechanism: Simple lagged heat is priced (Burke); the interactions (heat x own minutes, heat x age) and the 2026 cooling-break rule are untested and may not be priced.
data_paths: Open-Meteo archive (download); venue gazetteer (to build with Open-Meteo geocoding); data/studies/predictability_diagnostic/stage0_matches.parquet (minutes); the model's indoor input; data/dump/points/wta/events (heat suspensions 2019-26)
coverage_note: Outdoor main-tour matches 2013-26; ERA5 0.25 deg (~25 km) from 1940, ERA5-Land 0.1 deg; archived day-ahead forecasts (previous-runs API) for live-like inputs
prior_evidence: Burke et al. 2023 NBER (177,868 matches 2002-17: hotter previous match ~-0.1% win per C; 'most tennis betting markets appear to accurately price climate risk', incl. Pinnacle; R1 checked); Smith et al. 2018 (AO: doctor calls +47% per WBGT zone); Simani et al. 2026 MSSE (men's Slams 2000-25: older players relatively better in heat); ATP heat rule 2026
notes: Overlaps B1's RB07 and B3's MP-05; Burke lowers the prior; free tier is non-commercial (owner's call).

name: Edition court pace from Hawk-Eye bounces
definition: Per venue-edition, the ball's horizontal speed retained and vertical restitution at the bounce from Court Vision tracking of earlier days' matches (released by the clock), giving a pace-rating analogue; feature = this edition's index - the venue's previous edition, x (A's serve dominance - B's).
mechanism: Court changes shift serve dominance (Paris, Shanghai 2025 per media); ace-based pace lags; a physical measure is new information.
data_paths: data/raw/public_dump/atp_pipeline_handoff/court_vision/ (ATP 2021-24); data/dump/points/slam_ball_tracking/ (AO 2020-24, RG 2019-24); ATP Stats Centre 2025-26 (decryptable; Court Vision unverified)
coverage_note: ATP tour 2021-24 (4,570 matches), AO/RG 2019-24; none for WTA tour; 2025-26 unknown
prior_evidence: ITF (Capel-Davies & Spurr 2019): ~2 pace-rating points per km/h of post-bounce speed, return rate -1% per km/h (snippet); media court pace index Paris 46.6 -> 35.1, social-media sourced (SI 2025, R1 checked); B-VENUE z +2.50/+2.72 (ace-based)
notes: Formula of the ITF rating to verify at source (search cap).

name: Decline from own peak (men): serve speed and serve points
definition: Own 52-week mean first-serve speed minus own highest 52-week mean to date (system offsets as in the speed panel), and own 52-week opponent-adjusted serve points won minus own 3-year peak; A - B.
mechanism: The close over-rates older men; chronological age proxies a physical decline that varies by player.
coverage_note: Men tour level 2018/2021-26 (~49% of 2025-26 men's matches with ManTennisData), Slams 2015-26; women none
prior_evidence: Sutter et al. 2018 (serve speed peaks ~26, accuracy ~28, similar declines both sexes); Kovalchik 2014 (top players older, to 27.9 in 2012); repo: men's age vs price z -3.3 (2013-24)
notes: Thin before 2022.

name: Day-form volatility (pair steepness modulator)
definition: Per player, time-decayed SD of match-level serve and return point residuals (observed minus expected from pre-match profiles) over the last 25 matches; pair term (sd_A^2 + sd_B^2) x the close's log-odds.
mechanism: Match outcomes are over-dispersed; prices and inputs carry means only.
coverage_note: As box scores
prior_evidence: Sackmann 2014 (36% three-setters vs 44% predicted); De Paola & Scoppa 2017 (set-1 loser -20.5 pp in set 2 given average odds); Kovalchik & Reid 2019; repo: reliability family +0.232 [-0.038, +0.502] mLL beyond Pinnacle + profile (men, predictive_frontier); I-028 dropped (split-half 0.051)
exposed_2025_26: partly: predictive_frontier scored the reliability family through 2025
notes: Killed as a trait by I-028's split-half 0.051; listed to close it.

name: Early-retirement risk under each venue's settlement rule
definition: Shrunk 24-month retirement + walkover rate, a flag for a retirement or walkover in the last 30 days, WTA physio events in the previous match, and age; A - B.
mechanism: Pinnacle voids early retirements (rule to verify), Polymarket pays the advancing player: a venue-specific gap, not an outcome edge against the close.
coverage_note: Stage 0 every level; WTA physio events 2019-26
prior_evidence: Palau et al. 2024 (lower tiers: retirements 3.30% men, 2.73% women; +31% per 5 years of age); Sackmann 2012 (retirement rates persist by player); record 4.8% ATP 2025 (news); repo U-178 null vs the close
notes: For Polymarket accounting (B3), not for beating the close.

name: Recent withdrawal with an injury reason
definition: Flag for a withdrawal from, retirement in or walkover at an event in the last 28 days, split by stated reason (injury or illness vs schedule); A - B.
mechanism: The close has the news, the model does not: a defensive input that keeps the model from fighting a news-moved line, not an edge against the close.
data_paths: Wikipedia edition singles pages (withdrawn players with reason; withdrawals list) (download); data/studies/predictability_diagnostic/stage0_matches.parquet (status)
coverage_note: Main tour 2013-26, ~4,000 pages; reasons mostly given for would-be seeds
prior_evidence: Casals et al. 2025 (ATP walkovers: injury 28.7% of causes, unknown 61%); Sackmann 2025 (unreported injuries behind Elo-market gaps); George et al. 2019 (returns after surgery)
notes: Wikipedia probe receipts in receipts/wikipedia/.

name: Lucky-loser entry
definition: 1[entered as lucky loser] (and qualifier), A - B.
mechanism: Late entry and a reference-point loss; possibly a ranking lag the close already absorbs.
coverage_note: Every level
prior_evidence: Eckmann 2024 (Slam R1 1978-2023, rank-controlled: men's LL -0.40 log-odds, SE 0.13; qualifiers +0.40 to +0.67)
notes: B1's RB13 overlaps.

name: Pre-Slam effort and post-Slam letdown
definition: U-283 and U-284's definitions (top-20 at a 250/500 within 8 days of a Slam; a Slam QF+ within 21 days), A - B.
mechanism: Effort saving before a Slam; fatigue or relief after a deep run.
coverage_note: Main tour 2013-26
prior_evidence: Sackmann 2013 (61% vs 70%, raw); Sackmann 2014 (no general letdown; finalists ~1 pp worse); repo B-MOTIV z1 +2.39, z2 +0.49
notes: Failed replication in the pool.

name: Exposure to tiebreaks in the matchup (serve-dominance level)
definition: From the two players' predicted serve-point rates (profiles), P(at least one tiebreak) and expected tiebreaks under iid for the format, times the close's log-odds.
mechanism: When both hold easily, a skill edge converts less; the price may scale it imperfectly.
coverage_note: As profiles
prior_evidence: Newton & Keller 2005; O'Malley 2008; repo round-0 computed slopes 0.213 -> 0.175; Sackmann 2019 (aggressive pairs least predictable); Moskowitz SSAC 2025/26 (abstracts)
notes: feature_interactions measured the close close to the iid scaling (43% vs ~39%).

name: Night session and local start hour
definition: Local start hour (start_utc + venue time zone), 1[>= 18:00 local], and a day-to-night switch flag versus the player's previous match.
mechanism: Circadian effects on serving; night conditions (cooler, slower).
coverage_note: As RS07 start times
prior_evidence: Turner et al. 2022 and 2023 (lab; evening: more unforced errors, fewer winners)
notes: Thin evidence.

name: Eastward travel and jet lag (not recommended)
definition: Time zones crossed eastward since the previous event x days since arrival proxy; A - B.
mechanism: Circadian disruption.
coverage_note: All levels
prior_evidence: Maynard et al. 2025/26 (WTA: less sleep, no link to results); Song et al. 2017 (MLB, disputed); Leota et al. 2022 (NBA)
notes: Listed to close it.

name: Altitude and acclimatisation
definition: Venue elevation (Open-Meteo elevation/geocoding) and its change since the player's previous event, x serve profile.
mechanism: Thin air favours servers; arrivals from sea level may lag.
coverage_note: Probed: Bogota 2,582 m, Kitzbuhel 751-759 m
prior_evidence: Sanchez Pay et al. 2019 (122 ATP 250 matches: more aces at altitude); Sackmann 2013 (Sao Paulo ace factor 1.58)
notes: Venue pace already absorbs most.

name: Wind at the scheduled hour
definition: 10 m wind speed and gusts at the venue and hour (outdoor), x both players' first-serve reliance, and as a pair steepness term.
mechanism: Wind adds variance and penalises serve-reliant players.
coverage_note: Outdoor matches; reanalysis grid not stadium-level
prior_evidence: No study of match results found (lab side-wind serve study only)
notes: B3's MP-04.

name: Ball switch between consecutive events (not recommended)
definition: 1[the ball model differs from the player's previous event]; count of ball types in the last 4 weeks.
mechanism: Adaptation to ball changes.
coverage_note: ATP centralises balls by swing 2025-27
prior_evidence: ATP ball centralisation (2025, R1 checked: no per-event list); AP 2024 (10 brands, 19 types on WTA 2023)
notes: No evidence; variation removed by 2027.

name: Coaching change
definition: 1[a dated coach start or split in the last 90 days]; A - B.
mechanism: A change in level before ratings adjust.
prior_evidence: None found (not searched: cap)
notes: Low.

name: Women's serve-speed state
definition: As men's spd_L: 28-day minus long-run first-serve speed, A - B.
mechanism: State signal the men's model already uses.
coverage_note: WTA API advanced statistics 2021-26 (434 fields) hold no speed (R1 wta_fields.json); all courts tracked from 2026 (documented)
prior_evidence: Men's speed nudge (serve_speed_tabpfn)
notes: Blocked by data; ask SMT, WTA or Stats Perform.

name: Physical state from the rally (Hawk-Eye)
definition: Groundstroke speed, rally length and distance between hits against the player's own normal over the last 28 days; A - B.
mechanism: A physical state that box scores do not show.
data_paths: Court Vision (ATP 2021-24); slam_ball_tracking (AO/RG 2019-24); TDI rally length (2025-26 window)
coverage_note: Thin per player; 2025-26 ATP needs decryption (Court Vision unverified)
prior_evidence: Burke 2023 (heat shortens rallies, less distance run); Turner 2022 (evening: less distance run)
notes: point-shot-ideas #1.

name: Score-state resilience
definition: Per-player effects of being a set down or up and of the within-set lead on serve points (Kovalchik-Ingram model), pooled over 2-3 seasons; A - B.
mechanism: Response to the scoreboard is invisible in box scores.
coverage_note: Point-by-point matches only
prior_evidence: Kovalchik & Ingram 2016 (2015 Slams: ATP log loss 0.517 -> 0.509 with per-player effects; WTA none)
notes: Low prior.

name: Trust in the close (market-internal)
definition: Pinnacle's margin at the close; Pinnacle minus BetOnline de-vigged gap; books pricing; stale-close flag.
mechanism: Margins widen where information is unequal; a stale close carries less news.
coverage_note: Pinnacle closes end Sep 2025
prior_evidence: Barrutiabengoa et al. 2022 (higher margins on WTA, 51,881 matches); Abinzano et al. 2019
notes: Project policy: market-internal inputs only as uncertainty, never as direction.
